-   **IUCN:** Near Threatened
-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in shallow wetlands, marshes, and other open wet/muddy habitats.

## Natural history notes

A large shorebird characterized by its long bright yellow legs, slim body, slightly upturned bill, gray-brown upperparts, and white rump visible in flight. In Florida, it is found mostly in shallow wetlands, marshes, mudflats, flooded fields, pond edges, tidal flats, mangrove edges, and other open wet or muddy habitats, especially during migration and winter. It feeds mainly on small fish, aquatic insects, crustaceans, worms, and other invertebrates, often walking through shallow water while sweeping or stabbing with its bill.
